# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-12

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero earns the scroll — one clear jargon-free sentence and a relatable
"47 + 28 = 76" example. But the moment a skeptical stranger hits the Results
section (12 cards of FoVer / SVAMP / VeriCoT / CRANE / HalluGuard / PRM-BiasBench /
CCTU with a below-random 0.125 baseline and several perfect 1.0 / 60-of-60
scores) it reads as cherry-picked self-reported numbers, and they bounce. The
front door is good; the evidence wall undoes the trust the hero built.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. The Results grid is an unexplained-acronym wall (10+ undefined terms) — "What we measured"
2. "FoVer" is simultaneously the headline strength (0.9131 AUROC) and a defeated baseline (0.125 AUC) — stats bar vs Math-reasoning result card
3. Fabrication smells with no sample-size/CI anchor: 1.0 TP rate, 60/60, a 0.125 below-chance baseline — Results grid

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Honest read: per-card WORD counts are mostly fine. Longest bento body ("Why
  Energy-Based?") ≈75 words, under the 120 cap. No result card exceeds 60 words.
  Bloat is NOT the primary problem here.
- Results grid — 12 cards — borderline. Under the 20 hard cap, but each tag is
  jargon-dense, so a stranger skims all 12 and absorbs none. Suggest trimming to
  the 5-6 strongest with plain-English tags.
- Nav bar — 12 top-level links (Get Started, Tutorial, Concepts, API, Problem,
  Capabilities, Results, Quick Start, Report, Paper, Writing, Roadmap) — choice
  overload; mixes in-page anchors with external doc links indistinguishably.
- Hero "Recent progress" r-card (~47 words) is shoehorned INSIDE the
  `stats-bar` flex container after the 4 stat blocks — structural/layout smell,
  likely renders squished next to the numeric stats.

### Internal jargon
- Results grid tags — "FoVer", "SVAMP", "VeriCoT", "CoT", "GSM8K", "CRANE",
  "HalluGuard v3", "PRM-BiasBench", "CCTU", "EstimationVerifier", "HumanEval-50",
  "k=5 ensemble" — a stranger cannot parse a single one of these dataset/component
  names. This is the densest jargon on the page.
- Stats bar — "FoVer math step-errors" — FoVer is an unexplained dataset name in
  the single most prominent headline number.
- Hero "Recent progress" card — "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "architecture-only
  0.8947", "5-seed dual-condition" — "repinned" and "v2" are internal versioning;
  a stranger has no idea what was repinned or why two numbers exist.
- Safety result card — "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" — "publication gate" is an
  internal process term, meaningless externally.
- "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" capability card — "Process-Reward Energy Model
  (PREM) variance", "intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning" — the most
  internal-research-note card on the page; vague and grandiose, tells a stranger
  nothing they can DO.
- "AND-composed" (Multi-step reasoning) — minor, but unexplained.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Largely ABSENT — good. No ".120" / "2026.05.NNN" / "Milestone .94" anywhere;
  blog dates are real calendar dates. This category is clean.
- Adjacent residue only: internal version/artifact suffixes ("HalluGuard v3",
  "v2 0.9857", "HumanEval-50") — version-narrative-flavored, not milestone-number.

### Inconsistencies
- "FoVer" dual role: headline strength 0.9131 AUROC (stats bar + hero) vs defeated
  baseline 0.125 AUC (Math-reasoning card). Same name, opposite valence, no gloss
  that FoVer is a dataset used two ways — reads as self-contradiction.
- Three different code pass-rate deltas: "+3 points" (Code capability card &
  HumanEval result) vs "+18pp" (Ising-fuzzing HumanEval-50) vs "+15pp" (CRANE).
  Which is the real code improvement? The headline says +3, the results brag +18.
- Two "0.91" AUROCs presented without distinction: FoVer math step-errors 0.9131
  vs prompt-injection classifier 0.91 — a stranger conflates them.
- Meter-bar widths encode inconsistent quantities: "+3.0 points"→14.6% bar but
  "+4.9 points"→66.7% bar; "66→84% (+18pp)"→84% bar (encodes final value, not
  delta); "0.0pp accuracy delta"→95.6% bar (a zero-delta result shown as a near-full
  green bar). The bars actively mislead.
- Section label mismatch: "What you can check" contains 3 cards that are NOT checks
  — "Research operations" (how the project is built), "APIs & portable memory"
  (integration surfaces), "TTC & PREM" (a budget controller). Strangers reading
  "what you can check" then "Carnot is developed through an autonomous research
  loop" are confused.

### Missing essentials
- The three giant headline stats (3,406 experiment runs, 382 completed milestones,
  30,658 automated tests) are internal-PROCESS vanity metrics — they answer "how
  busy is the project," not "will it catch MY errors." A stranger cares about the
  latter; only the 4th stat (0.9131 AUROC) speaks to capability.
- No external validation. The "Preprint" section admits the arXiv submission "is
  prepared but pending operator-initiated upload" — i.e., not actually on arXiv,
  not peer-reviewed — yet the page offers "Read paper (PDF)" and "arXiv bundle"
  buttons that imply more external standing than exists.
- Maintainership: footer shows a single name ("© 2026 Ian Blenke"). One person +
  3,406 runs + 382 milestones + 30,658 tests can read as "solo, heavily
  AI-generated" — a trust question the page never addresses (no team, no
  institution, no contributors).
- Perfect-score result cards carry no sample size or confidence interval, so the
  "why should I trust this" question is unanswered exactly where trust is most at
  risk.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — perfect 1.0, no n, no CI.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100% on a 60-sample set, no anchor.
- "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC: 0.90 (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" — a 0.125 AUC is
  BELOW random (0.5); a below-chance baseline usually signals a label-flip bug or
  a baseline chosen to inflate the contrast. Strongest methodology smell on the page.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" — suspiciously clean (plausible for deterministic
  training, but unanchored).
- "0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings" (HalluGuard) — framed as a win but
  reads as "no improvement"; the 95.6% bar makes a null delta look like a triumph.
- Blog teaser "639 experiments self-verified … Zero false positives" — perfect zero.
- Reputational note: the blog row foregrounds "Caught Cheating: 95 Microseconds on
  a 30B Model", "Regex in an NTK Costume", "Two Retractions and a Rescue", and the
  "Research operations" card advertises a fabrication-detector on the project's OWN
  results. Transparency is admirable, but a 30-second stranger may read these
  prominent headlines as "this project keeps producing fake results."

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero one-liner is genuinely clear and jargon-free, and the concrete
  "47 + 28 = 76" example makes the value obvious to a non-specialist instantly.
- "How it works" (Extract → Check → Repair) is clean, well-paced, and almost
  jargon-free — the best section on the page.
- Install path, license (Apache 2.0), and a runnable code sample are all present
  and easy to find; honesty signals (provenance labeling, the two-AUROC retraction
  transparency, the external-reproducibility note) are a credibility asset if the
  noisy results section doesn't drown them.

2. Resolve the FoVer dual-role: drop the "0.125 FoVer baseline" comparison or add a

   and defeated baseline. Remove/explain the below-chance 0.125 baseline regardless.
3. Add sample sizes / CIs to every perfect-score card (1.0 TP, 60/60) or cut them —

4. Pick ONE headline code number and reconcile the +3 / +18 / +15 pp spread.
5. Replace the internal vanity stats (experiment runs, milestones, tests) with

6. Make the meter bars encode one consistent quantity (or remove them) — the current

7. Fix the hero "Recent progress" r-card wedged inside the stats-bar flex container.
8. Move "Research operations," "APIs & portable memory," and "TTC & PREM" out of the
